the relationship between the presence of a hernia and symptoms is poor:\na-Hiatus hernia is common in individuals who have no symptoms\nb-some symptomatic patients have only a very small or no hernia

qs.q: Which type of hiatus hernia is particularly associated with the development of gastro-esophageal reflux disease due to the loss of the normal pressure gradient and oblique angle?
qs.e: GERD is particularly associated with sliding hiatal hernia, which causes reflux because of the loss of the pressure gradient between cavities and the disappearance of the oblique angle between the cardia and esophagus. Paraesophageal hernias involve herniation alongside a normally positioned GE junction.
